chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) named a group who fasted when they broke their fast (as shortening the fast) as 'Al-'Usah' (the Shorteners/Deficient ones). He said, 'They are Al-'Usah until the Day of Resurrection, and we know their sons and the sons of their sons until our day today.'
ai.seo_question: Who are Al-'Usah in Shia hadith regarding fasting?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) identifies those who prematurely break their fast during travel or illness as 'Al-'Usah' (the Shorteners), a term denoting a specific spiritual status that persists until the Day of Resurrection. The Imam emphasizes the continuity of this lineage, noting that their descendants remain recognizable to this day, highlighting the enduring impact of this specific juristic classification in Shia tradition. This classification underscores the distinction between permissible shortening of fasts and the specific act of breaking them before the prescribed time, linking ritual precision to eternal identity.
